samples.summary: Fix for #1045 is knowingly partial: the same unrecoverable-undo data loss remains on the EditorAPI toolbar paths and Replace All. The new design-doc text states outright that `toggleList` / `indent` / `outdent` / `applyBlockStyle` (editor.ts:3612-3677, still `docStore.snapshot()` + an unbatched `forEachBlockInSelection` write per block) and `FindReplaceState.replaceAll()` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:69 — two writes per match, no batch) "lose their oldest writes exactly as the keyboard paths did before #1045", deferring them to issue #1048. Meanwhile the sibling toolbar path `applyStyleImpl` WAS fixed in this same diff (editor.ts, wrapped in `doc.batch`), so the change draws an arbitrary line through the same class of defect in the same file. If the issue's acceptance is "an action over a selection larger than the 50-entry cap must not destroy content", it is not met: Tab from the toolbar/menu, bullet toggling, and Replace All over a 100-block selection still permanently strand the earliest writes. Cost is user-visible content loss, hence major; confidence is low only because the issue text was not supplied and its acceptance may be scoped to typing alone.
samples.evidence: docs-collaboration.md new section "Not yet every multi-write action"; packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3632-3677; packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:69-76

samples.summary: An architecture change to the sharing subsystem ships with no update to its canonical design doc. The diff turns a share link from a fact resolved once at page load into a live capability re-resolved on a 60s interval (`SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, react-query `refetchInterval` + `refetchOnWindowFocus` in shared-document.tsx), makes `readOnly` a remount dependency for the docs / notes / slides views, and introduces a whole new client-side revocation mechanism (`revocableDocStore`, `EditorAPI.isDisposed()`, `neuterMutations` on dispose, `YorkieDocStore.dispose()`). `docs/design/sharing.md` is the canonical doc for exactly this — it currently says only "Revocation — Deleting a ShareLink immediately invalidates the token" and describes the Docs read-only story as decided at `initialize()` — and it is untouched. Only `docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md` was updated, and only about undo granularity. Per CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline the new mid-session downgrade + handle-revocation model belongs folded into sharing.md (and/or docs.md), not left undocumented.
samples.evidence: docs/design/sharing.md:163-219 (Docs read-only mode, Security/Revocation) unchanged; diff touches shared-document.tsx, docs-view.tsx, notes-view.tsx, slides-view.tsx, read-only.ts, editor.ts

samples.summary: Scope: the change bundles at least three independent concerns under an undo-granularity issue — (1) #1045 undo batching + undo-floor identity, (2) a new disposal/revocation model for the docs editor (revocableDocStore, isDisposed, neuterMutations, image-insert guards, YorkieDocStore.dispose), and (3) share-link periodic re-resolution with editor remount on role downgrade. (2) and (3) are a security/permissions feature with its own risk surface (a polling request per open tab, editors torn down and rebuilt mid-session) and no stated issue backing them in the material under review. Reviewing and reverting them independently is now impossible.
samples.evidence: diff spans packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts (new revocable store), frontend share-links polling, three view remount deps, plus the #1045 batching work

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.batch()` and `MemSlidesStore.batch()` are documented as mirrors of each other, but this change makes them diverge: MemDocStore now clears redo on write (`willWrite()`) and adopts an identical pre-existing checkpoint, while packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1789-1793 still pushes unconditionally and clears redo inside `batch()`. Two in-memory stores now answer the `snapshot(); batch(...)` ordering differently, and the surviving "Mirrors `MemSlidesStore.batch()`" comment is now false. No user impact today (slides text boxes run on MemDocStore), but the invariant a future reader will rely on is gone.

Duplicated batching logic across two layers: the toolbar path `applyStyleImpl` in editor.ts and `TextEditor.applyStyleToSelection` in text-editor.ts now each independently re-implement the same "cell-range vs range, wrap the store writes in one unit, then mark dirty and render" shape. The two must stay in step (the diff adds near-identical comments to both), and a future change to the undo-unit rule has to be made twice. A single shared helper (or routing the toolbar path through the TextEditor one) was available.
samples.evidence: editor.ts applyStyleImpl `doc.batch(() => applyStyleToCellRange(...))` vs text-editor.ts applyStyleToSelection `this.withUndoUnit(() => this.doc.applyInlineStyleToCells(...))`

samples.summary: Layering: `requestLayoutRefresh` is a new host seam whose implementation reaches into the host's incremental-layout invariant (save `dirtyBlockIds`, call `recomputeLayout()`, restore the set, mapping `undefined` to empty) purely to compensate for the TextEditor deferring paints. The knowledge of when the layout cache may be consulted now lives in two places (the seam in editor.ts and `computeLayout`'s `canUseCache`), coupled only by a long comment. A `recomputeLayout({ keepDirty: true })` option on the layout owner would keep the invariant in one place.
samples.evidence: textEditor.requestLayoutRefresh = () => { const dirty = dirtyBlockIds; recomputeLayout(); dirtyBlockIds = dirty ?? new Set(); }

samples.summary: The `snapshot(); batch(...)` collision is resolved by a value heuristic (JSON-stringify the whole document and adopt the top undo entry if it matches) rather than by an explicit contract on `DocStore`. That makes an ordering convention of `TextEditor` an implicit, structurally-compared property of one store implementation, and adds a second full-document stringify per batch on the keystroke path (slides text boxes, demo app). An explicit signal (e.g. `batch(fn, { adoptSnapshot: true })`, or having `snapshot()` record that it was the last write) would encode the intent instead of inferring it.
samples.evidence: const beforeJson = JSON.stringify(beforeClone); const adopted = top !== undefined && JSON.stringify(top) === beforeJson;

finding.summary: Indent/outdent/list-toggle logic is duplicated three times and only one copy got the undo unit, so the same user action now answers differently — and the toolbar copy keeps the #1045 data-loss shape
finding.evidence: `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` in `text-editor.ts:2815,2840` were wrapped in `withUndoUnit`, but the byte-for-byte equivalent logic in `editor.ts:3632 indent()` / `3656 outdent()` / `3612 toggleList()` (same `MAX_LIST_LEVEL = 8`, `INDENT_STEP = 36`, same `forEachBlockInSelection` loop) and the third copy in `text-box-editor.ts:1140,1163` were not. Result: Tab / Cmd+] over a 100-item list is one undo unit, while the *toolbar's* indent / bullet buttons over the same selection still issue one `doc.update()` per block — 100 units against Yorkie's 50-entry cap, i.e. exactly the unrecoverable-tail failure the issue is about, reachable through a different button for the same action. The new docs text (docs-collaboration.md, "Not yet every multi-write action") admits this and defers it to #1048, but the divergence is created by this change: before it, all copies behaved identically. The change also had to fix the inline-style path twice (`editor.ts` `applyStyleImpl` and `text-editor.ts` `applyStyleToSelection`), which is the same duplication showing up as double maintenance.
